sources.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
sources.text: Today, we’re announcing that NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart. You can deploy it with a few steps in SageMaker Studio or with a few lines of the SageMaker Python SDK. Super VL is the vision-language model (VLM) in the NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 family. It accepts images, video, and text as input and generates text. The model pairs a 120B-parameter hybrid Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language backbone with 12B active parameters and a C-RADIO vision encoder. It supports context lengths of up to 1 million tokens and includes a built-in Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) head that supports speculative decoding. You can configure reasoning per request. NVIDIA built Super VL for document intelligence, GUI understanding for computer-use agents, video question answering, and multimodal agentic applications. JumpStart offers two variants: NVFP4, quantized from BF16 with quantization-aware distillation for optimized inference, and the BF16 full-precision reference weights. In this post, we walk through the model’s capabilities and the JumpStart deployment configurations. We then show the measured inference performance and demonstrate text, image, and video inference. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a 120B-parameter model with 12B active parameters per token. It combines a hybrid language backbone with a dedicated vision encoder. The following table compares the specifications of the two variants available in JumpStart. Super VL is aimed at agentic workloads that must see and read. It targets vision-language agents that combine reasoning, coding, tool use, document understanding, and video understanding. The NVIDIA model cards report results for both checkpoints across reasoning, coding, agentic, long-context, and multimodal benchmarks, with evaluation settings held constant so that only the checkpoint differs. The following table highlights the multimodal benchmarks most relevant to vision-language workloads (reasoning on). NVFP4, the JumpStart default, matches BF16 on MMLongBench-Doc and stays within about one point on the others, scoring slightly higher on OCRBench v2 and OSWorld-Verified. For the full comparison against other publicly available models and the evaluation settings, see the NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Lightning Technical Report . We measured inference performance with the JumpStart release container using the generate workload profile: 250 input tokens, 1,500 output tokens, and five concurrent streaming requests. Throughput is the mean output tokens per second for each request, and time to first token is the mean across requests. These results illustrate the deployment choices available through JumpStart. The NVFP4 variant runs on G7 instances with a smaller GPU footprint. The BF16 variant on ml.p5en.48xlarge achieved 140.85 output tokens per second per request in this test. Time to first token remained about half a second across all three configurations. Because the variants run on different GPU systems and configurations, these measurements are not an isolated BF16-versus-NVFP4 precision comparison. Longer prompts change the picture: with the summarize profile (10,000 input tokens), time to first token on ml.g7.24xlarge is 12.62 seconds. SageMaker JumpStart supports Nemotron 3.5 Super VL on the following validated instance types. NVFP4 runs on G7 instances with NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, and BF16 runs on P5en instances with NVIDIA H200 GPUs. The JumpStart default instance for NVFP4 is ml.g7.24xlarge, which serves as the recommended starting point for the generate profile. The checkpoint includes the MTP head, but the JumpStart serving configuration does not enable speculative decoding. You can deploy the model from SageMaker Studio, with the SageMaker Python SDK, or from the Hugging Face model page. Before you deploy, make sure you have the following: To deploy the model from SageMaker Studio, complete the following steps: Figure 1: Searching for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL in SageMaker JumpStart Figure 2: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL NVFP4 model card in SageMaker JumpStart Choose BF16 if you need the full-precision reference weights on ml.p5en.48xlarge. The following screenshot shows the BF16 model card. Figure 3: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL BF16 model card in SageMaker JumpStart Figure 4: Reviewing Nemotron 3.5 Super VL capabilities and model details before deployment Figure 5: SageMaker endpoint deployment in progress before the status reaches InService The example uses the SageMaker Python SDK v3 classes: JumpStartConfig names the model, ModelBuilder builds and deploys it, and deploy returns an Endpoint resource. Pass the instance type in Compute , because the SDK falls back to ml.m5.large when the instance type is absent, and the build then fails. The deploy call waits until the endpoint is InService, which takes about 10 minutes on ml.g7.24xlarge. The inference_config_name argument selects a serving configuration, and each configuration sets a different context length. The default generate configurations serve a 2,275-token context sized for short prompts. The summarize configurations serve 13,650 tokens, and the modify configurations serve 15,600 tokens. The example uses a modify configuration because the inference examples in this post, especially image, video, and reasoning requests, need the larger context. All the inference examples that follow assume the modify configuration. You can also deploy the model from its Hugging Face model page: choose Deploy , then Amazon SageMaker AI , and continue to the SageMaker deployment workflow. sources.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
sources.text: Developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers can now try our latest frontier model. SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect, Google Today, we’re making Gemini 4 Carbon available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers. Carbon is our strongest model with frontier performance in cybersecurity capabilities and long-horizon agentic workflows across complex knowledge work, software engineering, and scientific reasoning. Two weeks ago , we released Carbon to a set of cybersecurity defenders via our Fairwind Program . Following our recent launch of Gemini 4 Argon , Carbon pushes the frontier even further. Argon remains the ideal choice for the majority of software engineering and knowledge work, while Carbon is built for tasks that test the limits of a model’s intelligence like complex, multi-step coding and debugging and open-ended scientific research and discovery — using more tokens than Argon to explore thoroughly, reason deeply, and run extended verification loops. Across independent benchmarks designed to test model performance in real workflows, Carbon pairs frontier accuracy with practical production economics. It ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0 , Perplexity’s WANDR , and Zapier’s AutomationBench at more than 2X lower cost per task compared to the next best external model. To put Carbon’s capabilities to work on larger and complex projects, we’re previewing /swarm in Google Antigravity, turning a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents you can track in real time. Developers can assign Carbon to roles that demand the deepest reasoning, like architectural design, coordination, and auditing, while pairing it with faster, lighter models across parallel isolated workspaces and adversarial verifiers that test every change. Gemini 4 Carbon is available via the API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business for all paying developers and enterprises, at the same introductory price 1 as Gemini 4 Argon ($2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens). It is also rolling out to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity , the Gemini app , and AI Mode in Search . Across legal, finance, and enterprise operations, Gemini 4 Carbon combines frontier visual understanding, reasoning, and exhaustive retrieval to synthesize grounded insights across large sets of dense documents and data. It follows strict schemas and formatting to generate polished and precise spreadsheets, presentations, and reports. Existing benchmarks don’t adequately capture how agents reason natively over dense files with charts, images, blueprints, schematics, and tables, so we partnered with Artificial Analysis to launch the new Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark that tests a model’s multimodal performance in agentic workflows. Carbon ranks #2 while being more than 6X lower in average cost per task compared to the top performing model. Using Google Antigravity’s new /swarm feature, a team of Gemini 4 Carbon agents turned historical photos and engineering plates into an interactive Three.js 3D exhibition of the Eiffel Tower's 1887–1889 construction from a single prompt. With seven public City Council planning PDFs (206 extracted engineering drawing views) and a single prompt, a multi-agent Carbon team using Google Antigravity’s /swarm feature built an interactive 906K-triangle Three.js reconstruction of Google’s Platform 37 office across 10 overnight loops. In Google Antigravity, Gemini 4 Carbon built an interactive multiscale textile visualizer based on an academic paper, modeling a virtual-fiber finite element framework with interactive 3D yarn meshes, 110-fiber polar tracking, and dynamic stress-strain curves with minimal prompting. In pre-release evaluations, Carbon matched the performance of the best model tested on deep financial research on Hebbia’s E2E Financial Agentic evaluation, and ranked at the top out of 23 frontier model configurations on Balyasny Asset Management’s General Financial Intelligence benchmark, spanning legal expertise, agentic tool use and execution, coding and data engineering, and perception and context understanding. Carbon performs exceptionally well on engineering tasks that require multi-agent collaboration like multi-package migrations, cross-subsystem root-cause investigations, and complex architectural redesigns. For web app development, it runs build-and-verify loops, recovers from errors, and checks both its code and the rendered UI to produce complete, working applications. Stronger visual design, spatial reasoning, and attention to environmental detail also carry over to 3D game development and creative coding. Using Google Antigravity’s /swarm feature, Carbon built an open-world 3D game where you explore Google’s Mountain View campus as a pelican riding a GBike — coordinating subagents to model 3D assets in Blender from Omni and Nano Banana references, build the browser game in Three.js with WebGL shaders, and pair procedural Web Audio sound effects with Lyria music. Try the live app . Paired with improved front end taste and motion design skills in Google Antigravity, Carbon reimagined the Google Merchandise Store in two prompts, proposing five art direction concepts and generating all-new product imagery with Nano Banana 2.1. Try the live app and Gemini front end design skill . Starting from a video reference generated with Gemini Omni in Google Antigravity, built a cinematic multi-shot underwater Atlantis scene. The pipeline modeled procedural ruins, volumetric caustic lighting, and water simulation in Blender before converting the full environment to Three.js for real-time browser rendering. Using a multi-agent loop in Google Antigravity, Carbon reconstructed a playable c. 1780 Stein-Schule fortepiano with 61-key escapement physics from CAD drawings and X-ray radiographs and placed it in a 3D model of the Royal Conservatory of Music's Koerner Hall in Toronto with seat-specific spatial acoustics. Try the live app . Gemini 4 Car

sources.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon with agent ‘swarm’ feature
sources.text: It ‘pushes the frontier even further’ than its last release, Argon.﻿ It ‘pushes the frontier even further’ than its last release, Argon.﻿ Google is rolling out its latest AI model, Gemini 4 Carbon, to the general public after releasing it to a select group of “cybersecurity defenders” two weeks ago. Google claims Carbon is its “strongest model” yet, and capable of competing with the very best systems from Anthropic and OpenAI. Google says Gemini 4 Carbon “pushes the frontier even further” than Argon, referring to the company’s other frontier model that launched only last month . The company said Argon will likely remain “the ideal choice for the majority of software engineering and knowledge work,” but that Carbon is “built for tasks that test the limits of a model’s intelligence,” such as complex, multi-step coding and open-ended scientific research. To highlight Carbon’s utility for long-horizon work involving AI agents, Google said it is also previewing a “swarm” feature on its agentic development platform Antigravity, which will let users turn a single prompt “into a coordinated team of agents.” Carbon is rolling out today via the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business for all paying developers and enterprises, Google said in a blog post. It will also be available to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, the AI Mode in Search, and on Antigravity. It is not clear when — or if — Carbon will be available to lower tier subscribers or free users. As with the launch of Argon, Google is pricing Carbon very competitively. The model is launching with an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, around a fifth the cost of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and a quarter the cost of Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 model, which launched yesterday . Even after those costs double at the end November — when the introductory period of lower prices finishes — Carbon will still be significantly cheaper than frontier rivals on a per-token basis, though this doesn’t necessarily translate to lower costs as models can use different numbers of tokens for the same tasks. Benchmarks cited by Google when it first announced Carbon suggest the model is one of the most powerful on the market across most metrics, behind Fable 5.2. It should be noted that companies can and do cherry-pick benchmark results to show their tools in the best possible light. The release, hot on the heels of Argon, marks a decisive return for Google at the very forefront of AI research . For months, frontier development looked like a two-horse race between Anthropic and OpenAI.

sources.title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon is now widely available around the world
sources.text: The company says it can be used for the most complex tasks, such as multi-step coding and scientific research. Google is making Gemini 4 Carbon accessible to more users after its initial release to select cybersecurity defense companies in late October. Gemini 4 Carbon promises a significant leap in AI coding and cybersecurity, as well as in scientific research. The company said that for most ordinary and even majority of software engineering tasks, Gemini 4 Argon still remains the better choice. Argon was the first Gemini 4 model and is considered less advanced than Carbon. Meanwhile, since Carbon was designed to test the limits of a model's intelligence, it's best used for multi-step coding, scientific research and discovery, as well as other more complex tasks. The company said that Carbon had helped its first users uncover zero-day vulnerabilities in a short span of time. It has also made advances in protein structure prediction, which is necessary for developing medications. Google is giving 10,000 scientists free access to Carbon for six months to help with their research — an initiative, which would presumably help train its models in turn — and has already onboarded thousands. Gemini 4 Carbon is now available in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business. Google AI Ultra subscribers paying $100 a month for membership will also get access to Carbon within the Gemini app, AI Model in Search and Antigravity, Google's agentic software development and AI coding platform.

sources.title: Google lanza Gemini 4 Carbon para todos: así es su modelo más potente
sources.text: Google ha anunciado el lanzamiento de Gemini 4 Carbon, la nueva versión de su IA que ya está disponible para desarrolladores, empresas, científicos y... usuarios en general, por lo que si eres usuario de la IA de la compañía, ya puedes probarlo. Hasta ahora, solo estaba disponible a través del Programa Fairwind y limitado para expertos en ciberseguridad. Según Google, es la evolución de Argon, siendo mucho más potente, pero la compañía afirma que Gemini Argon continúa siendo la opción idónea para la gran mayoría de las tareas, sobre todo en lo que a ingeniería de software y conocimiento; siendo Carbon un modelo mejor diseñado para tareas que, según Google, "desafían los límites de la inteligencia de un modelo", especialmente en lo que se refiere a la programación y depuración complejas. Respecto a los benchmarks del nuevo modelo, Gemini 4 Carbon ocupa el primer puesto en CursorBench 4.0, WANDR de Perplexity y AutomationBench de Zapier, y lo hace además con un coste por tarea mucho menor que el segundo modelo dentro del ranking, por lo que Google parece haber dado con la clave en cuanto a potencia y eficiencia. Si hablamos de costes, Gemini 4 Carbon llega con el mismo precio (de momento promocional y por su lanzamiento) que Gemini 4 Argon: $2 por millón de tókenes de entrada y $10 por millón de tókenes de salida. Una vez finalizado este período promocional, pasará a costar $4 dólares por millón de tókenes de entrada y $20 dólares por millón de tókenes de salida. Además, Gemini 4 Carbon también estará disponible para todos los suscriptores de Google AI Ultra en Google Antigravity, la aplicación Gemini y el Modo IA en la Búsqueda. Una cosa interesante de Gemini 4 Carbon son sus funcionalidades y capacidades extras de ciberseguridad, según Google, las mejores hasta la fecha, en especial en lo que se refiere a la seguridad de la inteligencia integral para el software crítico. Carbon lidera las principales evaluaciones comparativas en localización (SEC-bench Pro), explotación (ExploitGym) y corrección (CWE-bench v1) de vulnerabilidades. Es capaz de inspeccionar software, rastrear cómo pueden encadenarse los fallos a través de diferentes sistemas y generar parches verificados para subsanar la causa raíz.

sources.title: Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy further complicates Nvidia’s China problem
sources.text: Following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admission on Sunday to an extramarital affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, the chipmaker's relationship to China is about to come under intense scrutiny in Washington, D.C. Since October 2022, when the Biden administration announced sweeping controls to limit China's ability to obtain advanced U.S. chips, Nvidia has seen its business diminish in the world's second-largest economy. Months after an even stricter set of rules was implemented by the Trump administration, Huang said in October 2025, "We are 100% out of China." The recent allegations against Huang, while throwing the chipmaker into crisis, have also brought attention to the Nvidia CEO's potential influence over U.S. policy on chip sales to China, where its business once flourished. Of particular interest is whether restricted Nvidia chips have reached Chinese companies through customers like Singapore-based Megaspeed , the company linked to Alice Huang. The New York Times first reported that the Chinese businesswoman was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, according to people briefed on the intelligence circulated in a memo among the Trump administration in the spring. China has called the allegation a smear. Jensen Huang has been closely aligned with President Donald Trump during his second administration, helping advise the White House on artificial intelligence safety regulations, while also pushing for looser restrictions on selling AI chips to China. In December, Trump said Nvidia would be allowed to ship its H200 chips to China, provided the U.S. got a 25% cut of sales. In March, Huang told reporters that Nvidia had "received purchase orders, and we're in the process of restarting our manufacturing ." Huang was a last-minute addition to the roster of tech executives who joined Trump on a trip to China in May, after the president was briefed on intelligence concerns, according to the Times . "In 35 years, I haven't seen a chip CEO with this much direct influence on export policy," said Patrick Moorhead, CEO at Moor Insights & Strategy, in an email. Since last week's midterm elections that included sweeping victories across the country for Democrats, the mood in Washington has changed. Three House committees have requested closed-door briefings with the Nvidia CEO about his relationship with Megaspeed. Democratic lawmakers, who are about to take power in the House and Senate, have said publicly that Congress will investigate and seek answers. Trump said Monday that he was "amazed" by the allegations and that Huang told him he "had no idea that she was a spy." The FBI is now looking into the issue, Trump said at a White House briefing. It's been a long four years for Nvidia in China. Before the initial export controls in 2022, China made up nearly a quarter of Nvidia's revenue. Nvidia responded to the Biden-era restrictions by redesigning some of its products to comply with the new regulations. "It was a turbulent month or so as the company went upside down to re-engineer" the products, Huang told CNBC in a 2023 interview. Still, he was confident the company could continue selling chips to China. "I think we're going to be just fine in the ability to serve the customers there," he said. After the Biden administration tightened export restrictions again, Nvidia redesigned another AI graphics processing unit for China, the H20. Following reports that Chinese model developer DeepSeek was using restricted Nvidia chips, the Trump administration limited sales of H20. Nvidia revealed it would incur $5.5 billion in costs related to canceled orders for the redesigned chip. However, despite saying in its forecasts that "we're assuming 0% for China," the company maintained business in the region. In the last fiscal year, Nvidia reported that about 9% of its revenue came from China, including Hong Kong, although that includes revenue from segments outside of restricted data center chips, such as gaming, auto and industrial. Nvidia's China revenue was 8% in the most recent quarter. A report in May from short seller Culper Research alleged Nvidia's China exposure was much higher. The firm said that more than 20% of Nvidia's fiscal 2026 compute revenue was driven by China, supported by "illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries," according to the report. A loophole allows Chinese companies to rent Nvidia GPUs in data centers, even when they're restricted from buying them outright. For example, a Chinese company could lease Nvidia computing power in Europe by renting server capacity from a non-Chinese neocloud or data center operator that's exempt from export controls. Nvidia didn't respond to a request for comment for this story. Megaspeed , an Nvidia customer based in Singapore, has been accused of diverting its own supply of Nvidia's restricted AI chips to Chinese companies. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing and said inspections found no evidence of violations. In 2025, Nvidia changed the way it reported regional sales to categorize by customer headquarters, instead of by where the products were billed. Nvidia also stopped reporting Singapore sales during the same period. "Whether Blackwell chips reached China is a Megaspeed question that predates this week," said Moorhead, pointing to Bloomberg reporting in December 2025 that found Megaspeed had imported 50,000 more Nvidia chips than Nvidia tallied in its data centers. In 2025, a House Select Committee opened an investigation into whether China's DeepSeek operates on Nvidia's chips. A separate investigation by the U.S. Commerce Department was centered on Megaspeed. That probe was abruptly transferred to the Justice Department, the Times reported , following an email from Nvidia's general counsel to the Commerce Department seeking information about the investigation. sources.title: Jensen Huang’s net worth drops $6.5 billion as Nvidia stock slides in the fallout of spy affair scandal investigation
sources.text: New probes into Jensen Huang’s alleged relationship with a suspected Chinese spy have sent Nvidia stock sliding this week—and now, the billionaire CEO is no longer one of the 10 richest people in the world as his wealth continues to slide down the rankings. The day after the Nvidia cofounder confirmed he had been “unfaithful” to his wife, his wealth dropped by $6.5 billion. Meanwhile, his company’s stock fell by as much as 9% by Monday, winding up 4.3% lower at $178.67 per share. Huang owns around 870 million shares (roughly 3.5%) of the $4.3 trillion business in his own name and family trusts, according to a September 2026 filing, which represents the bulk of his fortune. The loss has sent him tumbling down the ultra-rich list past Walmart heirs Jim Walton and Rob Walton, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. But Huang is still worth a whopping $148 billion and is the 12th wealthiest person in the world. Fortune has reached out to Nvidia for comment. Investors and the public alike are reeling from the most recent investigations into Huang’s alleged spy affair scandal. Last month, the New York Times reported that the CEO had formed a relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, which buys Nvidia’s AI chips. On Sunday, Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation into the reports that Huang had been “the target of a foreign intelligence effort,” and the CEO sent an email to staffers apologizing for the extramarital affair. And just yesterday, Rosen Law firm filed a class-action lawsuit in federal court alleging that the company and its CEO failed to disclose information about Huang’s connections to the alleged Chinese spy accused of passing information to Beijing. “While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” Nvidia’s board of directors said in a statement. “Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.” The latest dip in Huang’s wealth only compounded upon pre-existing problems, as the CEO briefly dropped out of the top 10 last week after a broad tech stock sell-off following the Democrats’ midterm victories. But the pending investigations and lawsuits could continue to impact Nvidia’s stock and Huang’s net worth. Dan Ives, a tech analyst at Yorkville Ives, wrote in a research note that this is a “black eye moment” for the CEO and will create “an overhang” on the company’s stock. There are a myriad of concerns as Huang has an outsized influence on the company, U.S.-China tensions rage on, and the possible tighter export restrictions loom overhead. The net worths of CEOs and founders are largely at the whim of their company stock—all it takes is one breakout earnings report, scandal, or blockbuster news to shake up their fortunes. In 2022, notorious FTX cofounder and CEO Sam Bankman-Fried was dropped from the billionaires ranking after 94% of his fortune vanished in a single day. His wealth plummeted following Binance CEO Changpeng “CZ” Zhao announcing that he had reached a provisional agreement to acquire FTX amid insolvency concerns, leading to a freefall in the price of the crypto exchange’s native token. Just 24 hours before that, Bankman-Fried was estimated to be worth $15.2 billion, according to Bloomberg, losing $14.6 billion overnight. And in 2023, Zhao also watched his fortune take a hit. The U.S. government cracked down on crypto trading platforms Binance and Coinbase, which sent the fortune of its billionaire founders, Zhao and Brian Armstrong, on a downward spiral . The pair lost nearly $2 billion of their combined fortune after the Securities and Exchange Commission filed lawsuits alleging that both crypto exchanges operated unlawfully. On the flipside, good news can send a founder’s fortune soaring just as quickly. Michael Dell, the founder and CEO of pioneering tech company Dell Technologies , recently watched his wealth double thanks to the AI boom. The 61-year-old—who owns 40% of his tech company—gained around $122 billion between September 2025 and 2026, nearly doubling his wealth to a whopping $262 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. And earlier this year, Moderna cofounder Robert Langer re-entered the billionaires club following promising cancer vaccine trials that sent the company’s stock soaring. The “ Edison of Medicine” witnessed his equity in the biotech business double in value, shooting his net worth up to roughly $1.7 billion, according to an August Forbes analysis. His wealth surge followed news that Moderna and pharmaceutical company Merck’s mRNA cancer vaccine hit its goals in a Phase 3 trial targeting melanoma, sending Moderna’s stock soaring more than 100%.

sources.name: SiliconANGLE
sources.title: Trump stands by Nvidia boss Jensen Huang despite spy scandal, but FBI is investigating
sources.text: The revelations this weekend that Nvidia Corp. boss Jensen Huang had an extramarital affair with a woman who has been accused of working for Chinese intelligence have now ensnared U.S. President Donald Trump, raising further questions about national security. At the same time, the Federal Bureau of Investigation said it’s looking into the affair, meaning it’s likely to get continuing attention in coming weeks or longer. Nvidia said it has launched an investigation into Chief Executive Huang’s actions after he admitted to cheating on his wife with a woman known as Alice Huang (no relation), who serves as the CEO of a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed . U.S. intelligence officials suspect Alice Huang has been feeding information about Huang and the chipmaker’s plans to the Chinese government. And though Trump was informed of the possible infiltration, he has continued working with Nvidia and Huang on domestic policy issues related to technology and artificial intelligence, which have become of vital importance to the U.S. economy. Huang has spent the last two years cultivating a close relationship with Trump, gaining extraordinary access to America’s top decision-maker and influence over the country’s AI strategy. He has gone from being virtually unknown to the president to being a key member of a cadre of technology industry executives accompanying him on trips aboard Air Force One, including a visit to China in May. He has come to be seen as a major ally of Trump, attending numerous White House events while repeatedly praising his policies. Notably, his company made a $25 million donation to the president’s gaudy ballroom project, becoming its top corporate contributor alongside Apple Inc. Those efforts seem to have gone a long way toward getting Huang into the president’s good graces, and it seems to have paid off for the company. Last year, after months of lobbying from Huang and Nvidia, the Trump administration agreed that it could sell more advanced chips to China that were previously banned from being exported to the country. Though that decision was widely known, it seems that the Trump administration has intervened in other ways to protect Nvidia’s interests. Earlier today, the New York Times reported that a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed, which was suspected of smuggling banned chips into China, was abruptly canceled after receiving an email from Nvidia’s general counsel. Commerce official Jeff Kessler, who was nominated for the role by Trump, reportedly gave Nvidia permission to contact the investigation team and mention his name, which goes against standard protocol. Investigators had grown suspicious that Megaspeed was essentially just a front for smuggling embargoed Nvidia chips into China, but the correspondence from Nvidia’s general counsel Tim Teter kicked off a kerfuffle that ultimately led to the investigation being transferred to the Department of Justice. But Trump defended Huang late on Sunday, stating that the Nvidia boss is an “honorable guy” who has not committed any wrongdoing. The president had been briefed about the suspected Chinese intelligence operation as far back as October 2025, but decided not to do anything , according to the Times. “I haven’t heard that he’s done anything wrong,” Trump said. “He dealt with somebody, but, you know, so does everybody else.” Trump continued to defend Huang on Monday when quizzed about the situation again, before revealing that the Federal Bureau of Investigation is also looking into his relationship with the suspected spy. “I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he’ll be in good shape,” he said at a White House briefing. Despite the apparent protection afforded by Trump, Huang appears to be taking no chances. A report in Wired said today that the Nvidia boss has hired the services of a public relations firm called Heller that specializes in handling public scandals. Rise Heller, the firm’s founder, has developed a reputation for helping powerful men sidestep allegations of sexual misconduct and other personal controversies. She previously represented clients including the former Congressman Anthony Weiner, the writer Jeffrey Toobin and the chef Mario Batali, Wired reported. Tech industry personalities have also leapt to Huang’s defense. Shaun Maguire, a partner at the venture capital firm Sequoia Capital said in a post on X that Huang is “one of the greatest entrepreneurs of this generation,” and stressed that although he did something “incredibly dumb,” he believes there was “no bad intention.” Tesla Inc. CEO Elon Musk later shared Maguire’s post, saying he agrees with all of it. However, no intervention has managed to protect Nvidia’s stock, which slid more than 4% on Monday , wiping around $190 billion off of the company’s valuation. Nvidia is scheduled to hold its next financial earnings call on Nov. 17, in which Huang is likely to face some very difficult questions — if he is on the call as has been customary. sources.title: All roads lead to Jensen Huang. That's Nvidia's problem.
sources.text: Is Jensen Huang too important to lose his job? That's the key question tech insiders and market watchers are asking as Nvidia's board prepares to investigate whether its CEO was the target of a foreign intelligence effort . Some, like President Donald Trump , are supportive of Huang. Others, like The Future Fund investor Gary Black, think his days are numbered. (Meanwhile, the internet is just having fun roasting Huang .) BI's Sarah E. Needleman recapped the back-and-forth debate over Huang's job security. There are a lot of names to keep straight. Here's who's who in the Nvidia scandal. In the meantime, details continue to emerge about the woman at the center of the saga — Alice Huang . US intelligence officials reportedly believe Alice Huang (no relation) developed a close relationship with the Nvidia CEO and passed information to Beijing. Photos show the pair together at industry events dating back to 2024. The New York Times reported the Commerce Department halted an investigation into Megaspeed, the company Alice Huang has been an executive at, after an email from Nvidia's general counsel asking about the probe. And the Financial Times reported that Alice Huang and a business partner bragged to China-based investors they'd have "no problem securing GPUs." In a vacuum, the scandal reads damning for the average executive. But Jensen Huang isn't your average executive. How do you replace someone who's the face of your company AND an entire industry? Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters. That's the other big question tied to Jensen Huang's future. With dozens of direct reports , Huang isn't a figurehead-type leader. He's heavily involved in the day-to-day operations of Nvidia, a company he cofounded more than three decades ago. And then there's the wider position Nvidia holds in the AI ecosystem. Whether it's supplying chips, providing financing , or cutting deals , all roads lead back to Nvidia in the AI trade. So you're not just replacing a CEO. You're replacing the key person at the key company in an industry the economy is betting big on. (But no pressure.) Our Nvidia beat reporter, Geoff Weiss, has some analysis on who could succeed Huang if Nvidia decides to send him packing. Monday's market reaction was a bit convoluted. Nvidia finished down 4.3%, but the three major indices (S&P 500, Dow Jones, and Nasdaq) were all up over 2%. On Chinese social media, users have been tallying the cost of the fallout , from Nvidia investors to Huang's own fortune. Are investors confident Huang isn't going anywhere? Or do they think a Huang-less Nvidia won't upend the wider market? BI's Alistair Barr and Eugene Kim explain why Huang's scandal won't be a death knell to the AI trade . Don't expect Huang to weigh in anytime soon. He dropped out of two tech events he was scheduled to speak at this week. But he can't hide for long. Nvidia's next earnings report: November 17.

sources.title: Jensen Huang’s image has been shattered. Could he be pushed out at Nvidia?
sources.text: Huang built Nvidia as a family business but after the co-founder had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, its board faces a difficult decision For more than 30 years, Jensen Huang has been the seemingly unshakable public face of Nvidia. He co-founded the company as a young engineer in 1993 and oversaw its growth into a multitrillion dollar chipmaker and bellwether of the AI industry at large. He’s also made it a family business. His children, Madison and Spencer, have taken leadership roles at the firm. While not a company executive, his wife, Lori Mills Huang, leads the family foundation which, as of 2024, controls over 60m Nvidia shares. But Huang’s image as a family man has been shattered as of Sunday. After the New York Times revealed at the end of October that Huang may have been targeted by a Chinese intelligence asset who he had developed a close relationship with, he admitted in a letter to employees on Sunday that he had been having an affair. Initially , Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said there was nothing out of the ordinary about Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang , an executive at a Singaporean datacenter firm, Megaspeed. US government officials had suspected Huang of smuggling American chips into China, prompting those officials to surveil and monitor her, the Times first reported. In the course of that surveillance, officials allegedly determined that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy and had gotten close with the Nvidia leader. Nvidia’s board of directors have now launched an independent investigation about the national security concerns surrounding Huang’s relationship. “I support the investigation and will cooperate fully,” Huang wrote in his letter. “I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.” Megaspeed did not respond to a Guardian request for comment before publication. In his letter, Huang apologized to his family, acknowledging how much they’ve supported him. His wife, Mills, kept a relatively low profile and didn’t play a formal role at Nvidia. However, in a 2023 interview with the New Yorker, Huang shared that Mills had also worked in Silicon Valley as a microchips engineer before stepping away to raise their children. “Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support,” Huang wrote in his letter to employees. “They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it.” Both his children now hold high ranking roles at the company, despite not initially pursuing careers in tech. His daughter, Madison, serves as the senior director of product and technical marketing for physical AI platforms, but got her start as a chef. She attended the Culinary Institute of America and Le Cordon Bleu before going to business school and transitioning to luxury marketing. She previously worked at LVMH – the parent company of Lous Vuitton. Spencer , for his part, now serves as the director of product for Robotics at Nvidia but spent much of his career as a consultant before joining his father’s company as a product manager. Before consulting, he owned and co-founded a craft cocktail bar in Taiwan. In his letter, Huang reiterated his commitment to Nvidia, saying he hoped to earn back his colleagues’ and employees’ trust. However, analysts and investors say there’s a chance he may be removed as CEO after the board’s investigation. “This is a black eye moment for Jensen and will spark multiple congressional inquiries at a minimum and will create an overhang on the stock for a myriad of reasons,” said Dan Ives, a partner and analyst at investment bank Yorkville Ives. “There is clearly risk as discussed that Jensen could be removed as CEO depending on the board investigation and this will add risk to the stock as he is so important to the Nvidia story and strategy globally.” Ives said the family’s role at Nvidia adds some complexities for the board. “The board has to make its decision independent of the family spider web of Jensen and his family at Nvidia,” Ives told the Guardian. “It makes this a very complex situation for the board to navigate with the world watching.” Huang is to Nvidia what Steve Jobs was to Apple, said Ken Mahoney, the CEO and president of Mahoney Asset Management. “If you asked any Nvidia investor or anyone involved in tech and markets, would they like to see Jensen gone? Definitely not, but [Nvidia] would survive,” Mahoney said. “Losing Huang would introduce a lot of uncertainty, particularly given his influence over Nvidia’s strategy, culture, and relationships with major technology companies,” he continued. “The bigger question is whether a successor could maintain Huang’s strategic vision and ability to anticipate where the industry is heading, and how that new leader could be tested along the way if things become difficult.” Executive affairs or inappropriate relationships have recently unseated CEOs, according to executive recruiting and coaching firm Challenger Gray and Christmas. In 2024, the CEO of Astronomer was caught on a kiss cam with the company’s chief people officer, leading him to resign shortly after. Nestlé fired CEO Laurent Freixe for a relationship with a subordinate. Nvidia offers a more complex picture. On one hand, Huang’s affair is not just a matter morals or ethics, there are potential national security concerns. On the other, Huang is core to the DNA of Nvidia which in turn is the bedrock of the entire AI industry – an industry upon which the economy relies greatly. Nvidia shares fell 7.5% as soon as the stock market opened, wiping over $330bn off the company’s value. “When the CEO of the most valuable company in the world is tied to a counterintelligence investigation because of a personal relationship, every board in America should be paying attention,” said

sources.title: What could China get from Jensen Huang?
sources.text: The Nvidia CEO has been in a unique position to influence AI export controls. The Nvidia CEO has been in a unique position to influence AI export controls. It’s difficult to overstate Nvidia’s power in today’s AI landscape. The company’s chips are the bedrock upon which advanced AI technology in the US is being built, and demand has consistently outpaced supply for years. Nvidia has also been an influential investor in a wide range of up-and-coming AI companies in recent years, with about $99 billion worth of equity investments in frontier AI labs, neoclouds, infrastructure companies, and more. Its chief executive has even become close with President Donald Trump. This is why, as both cofounder and longtime CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang would be a valuable target for a foreign adversary with sights on the American AI industry. Huang is in hot water after news broke of his extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen) is an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud provider and a top Nvidia customer. Questions are swirling around how the affair may have influenced Huang’s reported push to sell advanced chips to China — and potentially even influenced President Trump’s own decisions surrounding AI export controls. Jensen Huang would be a valuable target for a foreign adversary with sights on the American AI industry US officials believe the Megaspeed executive is a foreign intelligence asset that has funneled information straight to the Chinese government, per The New York Times — in particular, officials reportedly believe that Megaspeed is related to a convoluted web of Chinese companies working together to access chips in bulk and perhaps even illegally get some of those chips into China. Alibaba is reportedly one of Megaspeed’s top customers. “It’s not entirely surprising that the CEO of arguably one of the most important, if not the most important, AI chip companies is the target of some sort of intelligence-gathering from countries like China,” Hanna Dohmen, a senior research analyst at CSET, said in an interview with The Verge , adding that an alleged spy would potentially be interested in “better understanding what the US government is thinking on export controls,” as well as gathering information on Huang’s conversations with the Trump administration, attempting to influence policy, and gathering information on trade secrets like “who’s buying Nvidia’s chips, who’s getting them first, what’s coming next in terms of AI chips.” Megaspeed’s sister company, headquartered in Malaysia, spent $4.8 billion or more on Nvidia chips and technology between June 2024 and February 2026, the Times reported, citing trade records from trade platform ImportGenius. The transaction sizes were outside the norm for a small company, particularly when Nvidia chips are so difficult to get. ”Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job” Nvidia spokespeople had said Huang’s relationship with the Megaspeed executive was strictly business. Their interactions were described as “not unusual or unexpected” in statements to the press. Nvidia’s line was, “Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job.” But at some point, their relationship became personal. In June 2024, just before Megaspeed became an Nvidia customer, photos show the two with other AI executives at a bar in Taipei after a local trade show; the following year, they reportedly had a business dinner in Taipei with others as well. But in private, according to US officials cited by the Times , the two’s relationship raised alarm bells for the US government — they had reportedly been surveilling the Megaspeed executive for months, if not longer, and that’s how it came out that she was in close contact with Huang. The revelation is particularly concerning because of Huang’s lobbying role. He’d been trying to convince the Trump administration and Congress to loosen export controls for sending advanced semiconductors to China, ostensibly so that Nvidia could sell more chips. We now know this was happening around the same time that Huang was spotted at the Taiwan dinner with Alice Huang in May 2025, according to Culper Research , which shorted Nvidia’s stock earlier this year. That dinner occurred shortly after Nvidia had shared the Trump administration’s new restrictions on its China-specific H20 chips in April. Just a couple months after the Taiwan dinner, Huang reportedly met with Trump in the Oval Office in July 2025 to plead his case for loosening export restrictions on Nvidia’s advanced semiconductors. Days later, the company announced that the administration had blessed sales of its H20 chips to China. Huang had argued that spreading American chips to China would help establish US technology as the standard, rather than allowing for Chinese chips to grow, according to The New York Times . After setbacks earlier in the second Trump term in export policy to China, Huang began speaking with then-White House AI czar David Sacks in 2025, who became the key advocate for Nvidia’s view that selling American chips to China would be beneficial, the Times reported. By October 2025, Huang was lobbying Trump to allow Nvidia to sell more advanced chips to China, ahead of Trump’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, per the Times ; but after Trump considered the proposal , he ultimately decided not to move forward. (That same month, Huang hired an external PR firm known for handling sex scandals, Wired reported.) Months later, in December 2025, Trump changed course slightly, allowing Nvidia to sell H20 chips to a greenlit list of “approved customers” in China, with the US government taking a 25 percent cut of those sales. The same rules would apply to other US chipmakers, he wrote on Truth Social at the time. “It is in Nvidia’s interest and in Jensen Huang’s interest to lobby for looser export control restrictions” CSET’s Dohmen said that during the past two years, the US has seen a light loosening of AI export

sources.title: Nvidia and Jensen Huang sued in US over affair with alleged Chinese spy
sources.text: California lawsuit comes as Donald Trump says FBI is investigating tech CEO’s links with Alice Huang Nvidia’s board needs to do some succession planning – sharpish Nvidia and its chief executive, Jensen Huang, have been accused of misleading shareholders in a lawsuit over the Chinese spying scandal engulfing the $4.3tn (£3.2tn) company. The legal action came as Donald Trump said the FBI was investigating Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy. According to a complaint filed in federal court in ​California, Nvidia and Huang misled shareholders in connection with the executive’s alleged ​affair with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based ⁠Megaspeed, who is not related to him. The lawsuit claims both parties did ​not disclose that the matter raised national security concerns that threatened the chipmaker’s reputation and business prospects. The New York Times reported on the alleged relationship last month, and said US authorities had concluded Alice Huang ​was a Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia described its executive’s interaction with Alice Huang as “not unusual or unexpected” in a comment submitted to the New York Times last month, adding that “meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year”. On Sunday, Huang admitted he had been “unfaithful” to his wife, without identifying the person involved in the affair. The lawsuit claims the NYT statement was “materially false and misleading at the time it was made because Jensen Huang had an affair with Alice Huang.” It also accused the company of making false and misleading statements about its relationship with Megaspeed, which has reportedly been investigated over suspicions that it may have been diverting Nvidia chips to China in contravention of US export restrictions. Huang said in an interview published on 30 October that “we’ve studied all their [Megaspeed] deployments of our GPUs and counted every one”. He added: “And I think the US government also has as well.” In a statement last year Megaspeed said it has acted “fully in compliance with all applicable laws, including US export control regulations”. Nvidia announced on Sunday it was conducting an independent investigation into reports that Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort”. Shares in the company fell on Monday, closing down 4.3%, reducing Nvidia’s ​market ⁠value by approximately $190bn. The lawsuit was filed five minutes after the US stock market closed. Nvidia and Megaspeed did not immediately respond to ​a request for comment on the lawsuit. Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has led the California company as it became the world’s most valuable chipmaker and made him ​one of the ​world’s most ⁠prominent symbols of the artificial intelligence boom. It is common for shareholders to ⁠sue ​companies after unexpected share price declines. ​Nvidia shareholders, led by Mark Kistenmacher, a retail investor, are seeking unspecified damages from the defendants in the class action suit, the term for a legal action where a person or small group of people sues an entity on behalf of a larger group. Several US law firms have announced investigations into whether Nvidia misled investors and have asked shareholders to get in touch. Trump said on Monday that the FBI is investigating Huang’s affair but said he did not think the executive had a reason to worry. “I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he’ll be in good shape,” Trump said at a White House briefing. “I did speak to him today just to see if he’s feeling all right, how you’re doing,” Trump said. “He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.” Huang said in an open letter posted on Nvidia’s website: “I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security,” The AI doomsday threat: Distinguishing facts from fear On Monday 30 November, join Dan Milmo, Prof Dame Wendy Hall and Stuart J Russel as they discuss the warnings surrounding artificial intelligence and how we can separate fact from speculation. sources.title: China panel chair Moolenaar demands answers on Nvidia CEO's alleged affair with a Chinese spy
sources.text: Rep. John Moolenaar , R-Mich., said on a Tuesday appearance on CNBC's "Squawk Box" that Congress needs to "get to the bottom" of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Moolenaar, who chairs the House Permanent Select Committee on China, said he wants to know whether Huang shared privileged information with a Chinese spy; whether Huang was influenced to lobby against preventing chip sales to China; and whether China was given preference in purchasing Nvidia's limited supply of advanced chips. And he urged a thorough internal investigation of Huang. "If it becomes less of an investigation, more of damage control, that's not going to work because people have to have confidence," Moolenaar said. "We're dealing with the country, the Chinese Communist Party that is a foremost adversary, that's funding wars and supporting Russia, supporting Iran, North Korea," he said. "And we have basically a Cold War race with technology. We cannot allow the premier company at the forefront of this to, in some way, be irresponsible." Congressional scrutiny of Huang's affair has intensified since members returned to Washington on Monday. The New York Times reported that Huang was romantically involved with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive who U.S. intelligence agencies have identified as a Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia opened an investigation into its CEO on Sunday. The two Huangs are not related. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries , D-N.Y., said in a press conference on Monday that "we're going to need a full briefing specifically as it relates to the Nvidia issue so we can all get to the bottom of what has happened and what the implications are in terms of national security" Moolenaar co-authored a letter with Florida Rep. Brian Mast and Arkansas Rep. Rick Crawford on Nov. 5 asking Huang to appear before the Select Committee on China, the House Foreign Affairs Committee and House Select Committee on Intelligence. Mast chairs the foreign affairs panel, and Crawford chairs intelligence. "Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the three Republicans wrote.

sources.title: Nvidia falls for second day as investors weigh fallout of CEO’s affair with alleged spy
sources.text: Nvidia shares sank a further 6% on Tuesday as investors continued to weigh the potential fallout from CEO Jensen Huang 's affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Shares closed more than 4% lower on Monday, the day after Huang told staff in an email that he had been "unfaithful" to his wife and had "fallen short" of his responsibilities as CEO. He reportedly had an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed , an Nvidia customer. The New York Times on Oct. 29 reported that U.S. officials had concluded she was "a Chinese intelligence asset, funneling information to Beijing" and "possibly steering advanced Nvidia A.I. chips to China." U.S. President Donald Trump said Monday that the FBI is investigating . "I've been reading a little bit about it over a period of time, but not too long ago," Trump told reporters at the White House . "We'll look into it. I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape." Adding to the tech giant's woes was a class-action shareholder lawsuit filed against Nvidia and Huang in federal court in San Jose, California. The Rosen Law Firm's suit alleges the defendants made false or misleading statements about his affair with Huang and Nvidia's relationship with Megaspeed, thereby presenting a material risk to the company's reputation and business prospects. "Right now the Street and investor chatter is assigning roughly a 15% chance he is removed as CEO of Nvidia with a high probability (85%) he stays on as CEO after the Board investigation is completed," said Dan Ives, senior and managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co, in a Tuesday note. "We would expect a Board investigation that could take 4 weeks to 6 weeks and will create a clear overhand on the stock until more news emerges from Nvidia." Amid Nvidia's turmoil, some of its chip rivals are seeing a boost. Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom looked to build on a strong start to the week, though shares pared gains in midday trading. AMD gained 13% on Monday, while Broadcom added just over 10%. — CNBC's Dan Mangan and Caleigh Keating contributed to this report.

sources.text: Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and potentially impact national security. United States officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company, had reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities. As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date. The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum. Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became a Nvidia preferred cloud partner giving it priority access to chips, the Information reported . The Info reported that Shanghai Century Litong. facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips. Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 US government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported . Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang. In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported. On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO. “I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said. When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia , Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.” Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife. “I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.” Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.” “Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote. Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day. Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees. “Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote . “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.” U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship. A Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary. “Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.” U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers which warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times. Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo. Around the same time, per the New York Times’ report , U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship to Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information. The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump , has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China. Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports. Mega

sources.title: Anthropic sets IPO range valuing it at up to $1.4 trillion amid AI stock sell-off
sources.text: AI lab Anthropic has launched the roadshow for its long-awaited initial public offering. The company announced a price range of $70 to $78 a share, a range that would value the AI lab at up to $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis, but is well short of the $2 trillion that some news outlets had reported just weeks ago. Anthropic filed confidentially in June and made its prospectus public on Oct. 26. SpaceX, which listed in June, had sought a valuation of about $1.75 trillion. Trading in Anthropic shares could start as early as Wednesday or Thursday next week. Anthropic is selling 825 million shares on the Nasdaq under the ticker “ANT,” which would raise up to $64.4 billion at the top of the range. Seven strategic partners, including Google and Nvidia , have also agreed to buy $26 billion of non-voting stock at the IPO price. Tuesday’s amended filing adds that Anthropic’s annualized revenue run rate reached about $81 billion as of the end of October, up from roughly $71 billion in late September. The IPO has landed at a difficult time for the broader AI industry. Following the Democrats’ major gains in the midterms, the AI sector has faced a sharp sell-off as fears over stricter regulation and tougher scrutiny, especially around the data center buildout, have spooked investors. The Nasdaq fell 5.5% last week and erased nearly $2.5 trillion in market value in a single session, as some analysts warned the market was tipping into correction territory. Instability at Nvidia, one of Anthropic’s key strategic partners, has added to the market jitters. The chipmaker’s shares closed down more than 4% on Monday after the company’s board opened an independent investigation in the wake of reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been the target of a Chinese intelligence-gathering effort, after he was romantically linked to a woman named Alice Huang. She served as an executive at Singapore-based cloud computing and data center company Megaspeed, and U.S. intelligence agents believe her to be to an asset of China’s main intelligence agency. Beijing has called the accusations baseless while Nvidia has said Jensen Huang fully supports the review. The market nerves around the midterms and Nvidia’s future add to earlier fears—often voiced by Anthropic—about the safety, and potential existential risk, of the AI systems the labs are building. Anthropic’s prospectus also carries a fresh warning about the company’s progress toward recursive self-improvement (RSI)— t he point at which AI systems become capable enough to substantially build their own successors, with each generation speeding up development of the next. RSI has been a long-held safety concern because that feedback loop could, in theory, push AI capabilities forward faster than humans can test, understand, or control them. Anthropic’s filing acknowledges the risk, warning that using AI to build more capable AI “could also pose a considerable safety risk, particularly if it sharply accelerates the pace of progress.” In a new amendment, Anthropic said internal estimates about future models indicate it “may imminently meet” its Responsible Scaling Policy’s definition of “dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI.” The policy pegs that threshold at roughly a doubling in the pace of AI progress, driven substantially by AI automating research. Anthropic said no current model has crossed it and that it is considering policy changes “to keep humans in control of frontier model development.”

sources.title: Anthropic sets IPO price range of $70 to $78 per share to reach an implied valuation of $1.404 trillion
sources.text: Anthropic intends to push ahead with its IPO despite shakier markets and the broader pullback from AI investing. The Claude-maker said in an updated IPO filing on Tuesday that it would be offering a total of 825 million Class A shares at an estimated price range of $70 to $78 per share. The sale is expected to raise anywhere from $57.75 billion to $64.35 billion. The company could end up being worth a hefty $1.404 trillion if its shares list at the top of the price range, on a fully diluted basis. That would represent a significant jump up from the $965 billion valuation Anthropic reached in a May fundraise , but it’s still lower than the $2 trillion the company was reportedly targeting a couple months ago. Separately, Anthropic said it had struck a deal to privately sell $26 billion of non-voting Class N stock at the IPO price to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC. Google and Nvidia are investing $10 billion apiece. All up, Anthropic estimates net proceeds to reach somewhere between $84.6 billion and $93.7 billion (the latter if the IPO underwriters exercise their option to buy additional shares). Underwriters, including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, will have the option to buy up to 123.75 million more shares from Anthropic at the IPO price. As a public benefit corporation, the founders hold a Class F share with 50.1% of the voting power. The Long-Term Benefit Trust will also elect a board majority, so Class A buyers will have limited influence. Anthropic intends to start trading on the Nasdaq close to November 19, per reporting from CNBC , under the ticker symbol “ANT”. The company expects up to 20% of the offering to be allocated to retail investors. Anthropic also gave out a few new details in the updated filing. The company said its run-rate revenue reached $81 billion by the end of October, about $10 billion more than at the end of September. Also, the filing now lists how many shares the company’s co-founders expect to sell in the IPO: CEO Dario Amodei, president and chairperson Daniela Amodei, chief compute officer Tom Brown, Anthropic Institute head Jack Clark, chief science officer Jared Kaplan, chief architect Sam McCandlish and interpretability research lead Christopher Olah are all selling nearly 3.4 million shares each. At the $74 midpoint of the IPO price range, that would land them about $250 million each. The updated filing also has a small but important change that hints at the company’s stance towards the Trump administration: the company at many points uses “super intelligence” and “SI” interchangeably with “artificial intelligence” and “AI,” citing Trump’s executive order from September that directed government departments and agencies to use that new terminology to refer to AI. The company’s third-quarter revenue came in at $17 billion, and nine-month revenue was $33.2 billion. The company reported a nine-month net loss of $104 billion, with compute and infrastructure commitments hitting $900.9 billion. It has nearly $132 billion in cash and short-term investments. OpenAI, Anthropic’s biggest rival, was reportedly valued at $1.25 trillion last week after it raised $11 billion, nearly half the $20 billion it had first tried to raise. sources.title: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion IPO
sources.text: Anthropic’s public offering is expected to make it one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies as soon as next week. Anthropic’s public offering is expected to make it one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies as soon as next week. Anthropic confirmed on Tuesday that its IPO could be one of the biggest ever, even while falling short of previous expectations. Its IPO price is expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share, which would put its valuation as high as $1.4 trillion, according to the The New York Times . The Wall Street Journal reports that according to its sources, Anthropic is “aiming for its shares to start trading Thursday or Friday next week.” As Reuters notes, the Anthropic IPO was previously expected to be valued at as much as $2 trillion. As of last week, Anthropic’s rival OpenAI was valued at $1.25 trillion . Those lower expectations follow months of debate around AI safety , and what that means, while midterm election results showed souring public opinion toward AI companies and data center projects they’re heavily investing in. And that doesn’t even include this past weekend’s revelations about an alleged Chinese spy’s involvement with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . The initial public offering price is expected to be between $70.00 and $78.00 per share. Anthropic has applied to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “ANT.”

stories.title: DeepSeek Harness cresce 545% e alcança 1,54 milhão de usuários
stories.summary: Plataforma de código aberto da DeepSeek cresce com versão desktop, quase 35 mil plugins e planos para criar marketplace próprio O post DeepSeek Harness cresce 545% e alcança 1,54 milhão de usuários apareceu primeiro em Olhar Digital .

sources.name: Olhar Digital IA
sources.title: DeepSeek Harness cresce 545% e alcança 1,54 milhão de usuários
sources.text: A plataforma DeepSeek Harness, voltada à criação e operação de agentes de inteligência artificial , alcançou 1,54 milhão de usuários diários e processa 92,1 trilhões de tokens a cada 24 horas, segundo dados oficiais divulgados pela startup chinesa no X. O crescimento foi impulsionado pelo lançamento da versão para computadores. A plataforma também soma 5,48 milhões de usuários ativos mensais e registra uma média de 261 requisições diárias por pessoa. Em poucas semanas, a quantidade de usuários ativos por dia aumentou 545%. No mesmo período, o consumo de tokens chegou a 92,1 trilhões por dia, alta de 306%. Tokens são unidades básicas utilizadas pelos modelos de inteligência artificial para processar e gerar informações. Entre os modelos associados à expansão está o V4.5-Flash. A comunidade de desenvolvedores também participa da expansão do ambiente. O Harness já reúne quase 35 mil plugins de terceiros, dos quais aproximadamente 30 mil estão hospedados no GitHub . Cerca de 59% dos usuários ativos constroem ou utilizam pelo menos uma extensão para automatizar atividades de trabalho. Conhecido pela sigla DSH, o DeepSeek Harness é uma estrutura de código aberto voltada à operação de agentes autônomos. Esses sistemas conseguem executar tarefas no computador sem depender de comandos humanos a cada etapa. Sob o lema “tudo é um plugin”, a plataforma permite que desenvolvedores externos adicionem ferramentas e recursos ao ambiente. A proposta é transformá-la em uma espécie de sistema operacional para agentes de inteligência artificial, no qual diferentes extensões ampliam as capacidades do assistente. Os números divulgados, porém, representam apenas o ecossistema do Harness, sem incluir os usuários do chat convencional da DeepSeek. Também não devem ser comparados diretamente aos indicadores de outros assistentes, que utilizam períodos diferentes de medição. O ChatGPT, por exemplo, registra mais de 1,2 bilhão de usuários semanais, enquanto o Claude também mantém presença entre os principais serviços do setor. Entre os recursos que podem ser incorporados à plataforma estão: Para ampliar o ecossistema, a startup anunciou a criação de um marketplace próprio, dedicado à descoberta e instalação de plugins. A iniciativa também prevê incentivos para desenvolvedores independentes e empresas interessadas em criar ferramentas para a plataforma. O programa deverá oferecer créditos gratuitos de computação, chamados de token grants, além de suporte técnico. Com essas medidas, a DeepSeek pretende estimular a criação de novas extensões e ampliar a participação de terceiros no desenvolvimento do Harness. Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

sources.title: Agente de IA da DeepSeek chega a 1,5 milhão de usuários em três meses
sources.text: O perigo de delegar compras para inteligência artificial O fim dos cliques na internet? Os agentes de inteligência artificial estão mudando a forma como navegamos, pesquisamos e fazemos compras no ambiente digital. Crédito: Pedro Castro A plataforma chinesa de inteligência artificial (IA) DeepSeek revelou alguns dados de uso do agente lançado pela companhia. Os números indicam que ela segue como um nome forte no setor, quase dois anos depois do primeiro grande produto. De acordo com o relatório postado pelo laboratório no X , a plataforma agêntica Harness já acumula: A quantidade de usuários é particularmente interessante: a base era de “apenas” 271 mil pessoas no fim de setembro , logo após o lançamento do aplicativo do agente de IA para computadores. Apesar de ter se popularizado inicialmente por IAs econômicas, o investimento da DeepSeek em capacidades agênticas de modelos seguem uma tendência observada em toda a indústria . Apesar da expansão, o momento da IA é de desconfiança do mercado — em especial sobre a viabilidade desses projetos a longo prazo, somando as previsões de gastos elevados e a demanda crescente por poder computacional.
